video_title: The Most BONEHEADED Play In Finals History Wasn't De'Aaron Fox

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the most boneheaded play in NBA Finals history
quotes.excerpt: The most boneheaded play in the history of the NBA Finals is that one.
quotes.quote: The most boneheaded play in the history of the NBA Finals is that one. That stopped a team from having the greatest championship in the history of the game of basketball. If we want to start laying out boneheaded plays, that was the biggest boneheaded play. Accumulation of flagrant fouls and then doing what happened in that moment. Golden State most likely was going to beat the Cavs. That was probably the Cavs' one chance to get a win when the mistake happened with JR.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on De'Aaron Fox's late-game mistake
quotes.excerpt: If you look at the De'Aaron Fox play two games ago, we'd be through it off of Castle's back.
quotes.quote: If you look at the De'Aaron Fox play two games ago, we'd be through it off of Castle's back. We'd be through the ball off of Castle's back. Everyone looks so focused on the singular moment of, 'Oh, well that play cost them the series.' Winby had a shot, he didn't make it, and two plays before they had the ball and he threw it off of his teammate's back in the backcourt.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on why the Spurs settled for threes against the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: They were moving bodies and the ball movement for San Antonio was immaculate in that first half.

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: One asking why were they continuing to settle for the three in the second half? They're up 29.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: They were moving bodies and the ball movement for San Antonio was immaculate in that first half. When they became exhausted, they're now settling for threes instead of driving to the hole, two feet in the paint, kick, swing, swing, swing. It's exhausting to play the level that they played, where New York said, 'You know what? We'll give you that open three because there's no fouls, we're keeping bodies on everyone, we're underneath everyone.' And the minute you start making or missing these, you're not putting pressure on their interior defense. What San Antonio was doing was moving New York left and right the whole first half. They were playing not to lose instead of playing to win.
